answer: Before entering the orchard, each agent must weave a vine from karst rock; the vine’s curl must precisely match the orchard’s living lattice. Any deviation forces a fresh chisel strike of 1.2 mm limestone per fake node, and the karst only chips once per meridian pass. Clusters spot identical vine curls by morning light, forcing farms to mine limestone at fixed delay—parallel runs jam in the narrow mouth of the cave.
